evidence: Accurate for the test federation provider. BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid (recovery-codes branch, ~lines 326-341 in the PR) deserializes the stored raw list and returns generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input)). It never removes the used code or writes anything back, so any code in the list is accepted and can be reused. getCredentials (~lines 230-252) rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(fullList, ...) on every call, so RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean / getNextRecoveryAuthnCode always asks for code #1 and allCodesUsed() is never true. Compare the built-in RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (services/.../credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:99-119): it only accepts the next code and then calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode() + updateStoredCredential. Also, RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80-87 calls removeStoredCredentialById for the exhausted case, which doesn't apply to federated credentials. Impact is limited to the testsuite fixture (testsuite-providers), not production code, but the fixture is the reference example and the new tests never check single use, so fixing it is optional.

The fact is correct. CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (server-spi-private/.../utils/CredentialHelper.java:~115-130) serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", type, json)). The local path uses credentialModel, which createFromValues hashes (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:65-74 via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode). The test provider then stores the raw JSON in credentialData (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java ~lines 193-200). However, this follows Keycloak's existing federation contract: passwords also reach CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential as raw challenge responses, and the storage provider is responsible for protecting them. So calling this a regression in the core code is overstated. Sending pre-hashed codes (or documenting that providers must hash) would be a reasonable hardening, but it isn't required.

server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:54 reads '@return - a optional  credential model', which has the wrong article and a double space. It's a trivial Javadoc fix with no functional impact.
